proof_summary: The key lemma constructs, whenever \(m\le s\) and \(\gcd(m,9)\mid s\), a multiple of \(m\) with digit sum \(s\): strip the powers of 2 and 5 from \(m\), use \(10^{\varphi(m')}\equiv1\pmod{m'}\) and a solution of \(9y+s\equiv0\pmod{m'}\) to place digit blocks of total weights \(s-y\) and \(y\) in exponent classes 0 and 1, then append zeros to restore the stripped factors (with the divisors of 9 handled by repeated 1s). Applying this with \(s=n\) and \(m=D(n)\) works because \(n\equiv D(n)\pmod 9\); for \(n\ge10\), \(D(n)<n\) makes the constructed partner distinct, while for \(n<10\) the partner \(10n\) suffices.
